4	`ARCHITECTURE.md`; every setting is in `CONFIGURATION.md`.
5	
6	## What this module is
7	
8	The Spring Boot service behind the ALB. Accepts `PUT /logs/<file>`, checks headers only, streams the body to S3 with a
9	create-only write, and answers 200 once S3 confirms. `HEAD /logs/<file>` is always 404.
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	From the repo root:
14	
15	- Build and test this module (`-am` also builds the contract): `mvn -pl upload-service -am verify`
16	- Run locally after a build, with no config server or discovery:
17	  `java -jar upload-service/target/device-log-upload-service.jar --spring.profiles.active=local-test`. App on 1296,
18	  management on 1297. Without `local-test` the jar exits at startup because no config server answers (failFast).
19	- Check it from a second terminal. The path is `/logs/<file>`, not `/public/logs/<file>`, which also gives 404 but
20	  from no handler:
21	
22	  ```
23	  curl -I localhost:1296/logs/0004f2abcdef-app.log                             # 404, from LogUploadController
24	  curl -i -X PUT --data-binary hello localhost:1296/logs/not-a-log-name        # 400, bad file name
25	  curl -i -X PUT --data-binary hello localhost:1296/logs/0004f2abcdef-app.log  # 403, no ALB headers
26	  curl -i localhost:1296/public/ping                                           # 200, body pong
27	  curl -i localhost:1296/other                                                 # 401, cloud8 security still on
28	  curl -s localhost:1297/actuator/health                                       # {"status":"UP",...}
29	  ```
30	
31	- Integration tests against LocalStack (`*IT` under `src/test-integration/java`, Docker needed): Failsafe runs them in
32	  `mvn -pl upload-service -am verify`, in a JVM capped at 256 MB so `UploadIT` proves a 500 MB body streams.
33	- An allowed upload needs S3. With the `local-test` profile it goes to LocalStack on localhost:4566, bucket
34	  `device-logs-local`; without LocalStack running it gets 429.
35	
36	## Package map
37	
38	One line per package, matching its `package-info.java`:
39	
40	- `web`: HTTP only. Maps every `Rejection` to its status code in one place.
41	- `trust`: the only code that reads ALB mTLS and X-Forwarded-For headers.
42	- `policy`: the checks that need no body, in the order `openapi.yaml` lists them.
43	- `ratelimit`: the `RateLimiter` interface and its in-memory implementation. Not wired yet (ADR 0010).
44	- `upload`: runs one upload end to end and returns one `UploadOutcome`.
45	- `storage`: the `LogStorage` interface. `storage.s3`: its only S3 implementation.
46	- `config`: `DeviceLogsProperties`, validated at startup.
47	- `metrics`: `UploadMetrics`, the only place meters are created. A placeholder today.
48	
49	## Hard rules
50	
51	- Nothing reads the request body before every check has passed. Tomcat sends 100 Continue on the first read, but only
52	  because `web/ContinueOnReadCustomizer` sets it; its default sends it before any check runs.
53	  `ExpectContinueOnTomcatTest` fails if either breaks (ADR 0009).
54	- Never return 503. Overload and storage problems are 429 (ADR 0009).
55	- Only `trust` reads `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` or `X-Forwarded-For`. Header names come from config (ADR 0004).
56	- Only `storage.s3` imports AWS SDK classes (ADR 0013).
57	- Never log or store the body anywhere but S3. One structured log line per request, without contents.
58	
59	## ADRs that bind this module
60	
61	- ADR 0001: no ingress template in the chart; ALB settings are annotations in values.yaml.
62	- ADR 0002: no ACM-issued certificate without lab proof phones trust the Amazon root.
63	- ADR 0003: don't tighten the TLS policy without checking ALB connection logs.
64	- ADR 0004: only `trust/AlbHeaderTrust` reads the ALB headers; names from config.
65	- ADR 0005: S3 write timeout, ALB idle timeout and Tomcat keep-alive change together, in that order.
66	- ADR 0006: don't turn cloud8 security off; only `/logs/**` and `/public/**` are public.
67	- ADR 0007: a new file type is a contract change, vectors and a config default together.
68	- ADR 0008: never enable calls.xml by default.
69	- ADR 0009: never 503; never read the body before every check passes.
70	- ADR 0010: callers use the `RateLimiter` interface; no network call on the upload path.
71	- ADR 0011: never write to S3 without `If-None-Match: *`.
72	- ADR 0012: no role-arn annotation on the service account; no AWS keys in config.
73	- ADR 0013: AWS SDK v2 only.
74	- ADR 0015: deploy into `herd-endpoints`; don't create a namespace.
75	
76	## When ...
77	
78	- When adding a rejection: `policy/Rejection.java`, `web/RejectionStatusMapper.java`, `openapi.yaml` and the
79	  parameterized `LogUploadControllerTest`, together.
80	- When adding a setting: `config/DeviceLogsProperties.java`, `application.yml`, and the row in `CONFIGURATION.md`.
81	- When changing a Helm value: say in the PR whether it is a repo default or set per environment in GDS.
82	- When adding a meter: `metrics/UploadMetrics.java` only, and its row in `docs/operations/observability.md`.
83	
84	## Tests
85	
86	- Unit tests (Surefire, `src/test/java`): header trust (duplicate or missing headers, leaf versus Subject mismatch,
87	  X-Forwarded-For forms), policy, the upload flow with the in-memory `LogStorage` fake and a fixed `Clock`, and
88	  config validation. Never real S3.
89	- Web-slice tests (MockMvc): every status code in `openapi.yaml` in one parameterized test, HEAD always 404, and proof
90	  the body is not read when a check fails.
91	- Integration tests (Failsafe, `src/test-integration/java`, Testcontainers LocalStack): the S3 adapter's object,
92	  metadata and create-only behaviour; the full app over real HTTP with ALB-style headers; a 500 MB upload in a 256 MB
93	  heap; a phone that closes or goes quiet mid-body getting Tomcat's own 400 or 408, logged as that code, not 429.

# upload-service/CLAUDE.md

Rules for agents working in `upload-service`. The root CLAUDE.md still applies. How the service is put together is in
`ARCHITECTURE.md`; every setting is in `CONFIGURATION.md`.

## What this module is

The Spring Boot service behind the ALB. Accepts `PUT /logs/<file>`, checks headers only, streams the body to S3 with a
create-only write, and answers 200 once S3 confirms. `HEAD /logs/<file>` is always 404.

## Commands

From the repo root:

- Build and test this module (`-am` also builds the contract): `mvn -pl upload-service -am verify`
- Run locally after a build, with no config server or discovery:
  `java -jar upload-service/target/device-log-upload-service.jar --spring.profiles.active=local-test`. App on 1296,
  management on 1297. Without `local-test` the jar exits at startup because no config server answers (failFast).
- Check it from a second terminal. The path is `/logs/<file>`, not `/public/logs/<file>`, which also gives 404 but
  from no handler:

  ```
  curl -I localhost:1296/logs/0004f2abcdef-app.log                             # 404, from LogUploadController
  curl -i -X PUT --data-binary hello localhost:1296/logs/not-a-log-name        # 400, bad file name
  curl -i -X PUT --data-binary hello localhost:1296/logs/0004f2abcdef-app.log  # 403, no ALB headers
  curl -i localhost:1296/public/ping                                           # 200, body pong
  curl -i localhost:1296/other                                                 # 401, cloud8 security still on
  curl -s localhost:1297/actuator/health                                       # {"status":"UP",...}
  ```

- Integration tests against LocalStack (`*IT` under `src/test-integration/java`, Docker needed): Failsafe runs them in
  `mvn -pl upload-service -am verify`, in a JVM capped at 256 MB so `UploadIT` proves a 500 MB body streams.
- An allowed upload needs S3. With the `local-test` profile it goes to LocalStack on localhost:4566, bucket
  `device-logs-local`; without LocalStack running it gets 429.

## Package map

One line per package, matching its `package-info.java`:

- `web`: HTTP only. Maps every `Rejection` to its status code in one place.
- `trust`: the only code that reads ALB mTLS and X-Forwarded-For headers.
- `policy`: the checks that need no body, in the order `openapi.yaml` lists them.
- `ratelimit`: the `RateLimiter` interface and its in-memory implementation. Not wired yet (ADR 0010).
- `upload`: runs one upload end to end and returns one `UploadOutcome`.
- `storage`: the `LogStorage` interface. `storage.s3`: its only S3 implementation.
- `config`: `DeviceLogsProperties`, validated at startup.
- `metrics`: `UploadMetrics`, the only place meters are created. A placeholder today.

## Hard rules

- Nothing reads the request body before every check has passed. Tomcat sends 100 Continue on the first read, but only
  because `web/ContinueOnReadCustomizer` sets it; its default sends it before any check runs.
  `ExpectContinueOnTomcatTest` fails if either breaks (ADR 0009).
- Never return 503. Overload and storage problems are 429 (ADR 0009).
- Only `trust` reads `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` or `X-Forwarded-For`. Header names come from config (ADR 0004).
- Only `storage.s3` imports AWS SDK classes (ADR 0013).
- Never log or store the body anywhere but S3. One structured log line per request, without contents.

## ADRs that bind this module

- ADR 0001: no ingress template in the chart; ALB settings are annotations in values.yaml.
- ADR 0002: no ACM-issued certificate without lab proof phones trust the Amazon root.
- ADR 0003: don't tighten the TLS policy without checking ALB connection logs.
- ADR 0004: only `trust/AlbHeaderTrust` reads the ALB headers; names from config.
- ADR 0005: S3 write timeout, ALB idle timeout and Tomcat keep-alive change together, in that order.
- ADR 0006: don't turn cloud8 security off; only `/logs/**` and `/public/**` are public.
- ADR 0007: a new file type is a contract change, vectors and a config default together.
- ADR 0008: never enable calls.xml by default.
- ADR 0009: never 503; never read the body before every check passes.
- ADR 0010: callers use the `RateLimiter` interface; no network call on the upload path.
- ADR 0011: never write to S3 without `If-None-Match: *`.
- ADR 0012: no role-arn annotation on the service account; no AWS keys in config.
- ADR 0013: AWS SDK v2 only.
- ADR 0015: deploy into `herd-endpoints`; don't create a namespace.

## When ...

- When adding a rejection: `policy/Rejection.java`, `web/RejectionStatusMapper.java`, `openapi.yaml` and the
  parameterized `LogUploadControllerTest`, together.
- When adding a setting: `config/DeviceLogsProperties.java`, `application.yml`, and the row in `CONFIGURATION.md`.
- When changing a Helm value: say in the PR whether it is a repo default or set per environment in GDS.
- When adding a meter: `metrics/UploadMetrics.java` only, and its row in `docs/operations/observability.md`.

## Tests

- Unit tests (Surefire, `src/test/java`): header trust (duplicate or missing headers, leaf versus Subject mismatch,
  X-Forwarded-For forms), policy, the upload flow with the in-memory `LogStorage` fake and a fixed `Clock`, and
  config validation. Never real S3.
- Web-slice tests (MockMvc): every status code in `openapi.yaml` in one parameterized test, HEAD always 404, and proof
  the body is not read when a check fails.
- Integration tests (Failsafe, `src/test-integration/java`, Testcontainers LocalStack): the S3 adapter's object,
  metadata and create-only behaviour; the full app over real HTTP with ALB-style headers; a 500 MB upload in a 256 MB
  heap; a phone that closes or goes quiet mid-body getting Tomcat's own 400 or 408, logged as that code, not 429.

1	package com._8x8.herd.device_logs.upload.policy;
2	
3	/**
4	 * Why an upload is refused: one reason per check in {@link UploadPolicy}, then what can go wrong once the body is read,
5	 * in {@code upload.UploadFlow}. Each reason has its status code in {@code web.RejectionStatusMapper} and its response
6	 * in openapi.yaml, so adding one means updating both, and the parameterized web test.
7	 */
8	public enum Rejection {
9	
10	    /** The path after /logs/ is not an accepted file name. 400. */
11	    BAD_FILE_NAME,
12	
13	    /** The file type is turned off in device-logs.file-types, as calls.xml is by default. 403. */
14	    FILE_TYPE_DISABLED,
15	
16	    /** The ALB headers do not establish who is calling. 403. */
17	    UNTRUSTED_IDENTITY,
18	
19	    /** The certificate MAC differs from the MAC in the file name. 403. */
20	    MAC_MISMATCH,
21	
22	    /** The request has no Content-Length, for example because it is chunked. 411. */
23	    LENGTH_REQUIRED,
24	
25	    /** Content-Length is above the type's max-size. 413. */
26	    TOO_LARGE,
27	
28	    /**
29	     * The connection ended before Content-Length bytes arrived. Tomcat answers 400 itself when its read of the body
30	     * fails, so this records the same code.
31	     */
32	    BODY_INCOMPLETE,
33	
34	    /** The body stopped arriving for longer than Tomcat's connection timeout. Tomcat answers 408 itself, as above. */
35	    BODY_TIMEOUT,
36	
37	    /** An object already has this key, so the create-only write was refused and nothing was overwritten. 429. */
38	    KEY_EXISTS,
39	
40	    /** The write to storage failed or ran past its deadline. The file may still have been stored. 429, never 503. */
41	    STORAGE_FAILED
42	}
43

You need to change these four files together:

1. **`upload-service/src/main/java/com/_8x8/herd/device_logs/upload/policy/Rejection.java`**: add the enum value, with a Javadoc line giving its status code.
2. **`upload-service/src/main/java/com/_8x8/herd/device_logs/upload/web/RejectionStatusMapper.java`**: map the new value to its HTTP status. The switch has no default, so the build fails until you do this. The status can never be 503; overload and storage problems get 429 (ADR 0009).
3. **`upload-service/openapi.yaml`**: add the response. If the status code is new, also follow the root rule for adding or changing a status code.
4. **`upload-service/src/test/java/com/_8x8/herd/device_logs/upload/web/LogUploadControllerTest.java`**: add a case to the parameterized test.

You'll also need the code that returns the new reason, which none of the docs list:
- **`policy/UploadPolicy.java`** for a header check. Every check must run before the body is read (ADR 0009).
- **`upload/UploadFlow`** for something that goes wrong after the body is read.

Its unit test goes in the same package under `src/test/java`, for example `policy/UploadPolicyTest.java`.

Files used:
- `CLAUDE.md` (the "Where new code goes" table and the architecture rules)
- `upload-service/CLAUDE.md` ("When adding a rejection")
- `upload-service/src/main/java/com/_8x8/herd/device_logs/upload/policy/Rejection.java`
- `upload-service/src/main/java/com/_8x8/herd/device_logs/upload/web/RejectionStatusMapper.java`
